summary: Dayong (1893-1929) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Bai Puren, Dorje Geshe, and Palden Tenzin Nyendrak. He taught at Wuchang Buddhist Institute and founded the Tibetan Language School of Beijing.

Debala Mitra (1925-2003) specialized in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Dineschandra Sircar and served as Director at the Archaeological Survey of India from circa 1952 to 1983.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak (born 1931) is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Cornell University from circa 1959 to 1961 and served as Director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages from circa 1969 to 1989.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918-1993) worked in philosophy, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Calcutta from circa 1937 to 1942, including under Surendranath Dasgupta, and later held a post at the University of Calcutta.
Deborah Carlson is a scholar in history and archaeology. She held posts at Texas A&M University around 2004 and at the Institute of Nautical Archaeology from circa 2011 to 2020.

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is a scholar of history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Vienna and Harvard University under Oleg Grabar. She served as Professor at the University of Vienna from circa 1996 to 2013.
Declan Quigley works in Indology and other fields. He has held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei (born 1968) works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Renmin University of China (~1994-1998) and became an associate professor of religious studies there around 1998.

Denis Sinor (1916-2011) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history and archaeology. After studying at Cambridge in 1948, he held posts at Cambridge and Indiana University, where he directed programs and edited the Uralic and Altaic Series.

Denis Twitchett (1925-2006) was a scholar of Sinology and history. He studied at St Catharine's College and SOAS University of London, and held professorships at the University of London and the University of Cambridge before becoming emeritus at Princeton University.

Denma Lochö Rinpoche (1928-2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery from circa 1939 to 1959 and was a Visiting Scholar at the University of Virginia from circa 1978 to 1979.
Dennis A. Johnson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna by 2012 under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Dennis Hirota (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned degrees from the University of California, Berkeley and Nagoya University, and held posts at the Hongwanji International Center and Ryukoku University as Professor in the Faculty of Letters.

Derek F. Maher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his B.A. from Evergreen State College and Ph.D. from the University of Virginia, later lecturing there and at UNC Greensboro, and co-directing Religious Studies at East Carolina University.

Derek Parfit (1942-2017) was a philosopher who studied at Eton College and Balliol College. He held academic posts at All Souls College from circa 1967 to 2017, as well as New York University and Harvard University.

Dermot Killingley (born 1935) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Oxford and SOAS, and held posts at the University of Malaya and Newcastle University, where he was Senior Lecturer and Reader in Religious Studies.

Dermott Joseph Walsh specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a BA at Trinity College Dublin, an MA at Leiden University, and a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles under William M. Bodiford.

Devadatta Ramkrishna Bhandarkar (1875-1950) was a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. He served as Superintendent of the Western Circle at the Archaeological Survey of India (1911-1917) and Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta in 1928.
Dewei Zhang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia between circa 2004 and 2010 under the supervision of Jinhua Chen.

Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima (1906-1987) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Nyima, Gatön Ngawang Lekpa, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, and participated in a research project at the University of Washington (1960-1986).
